summary.one_liner: A curated, link-only collection of step-by-step tutorials for re-creating technologies such as databases, compilers, shells, operating systems, and blockchains from scratch.
summary.what_it_does: This is an awesome-style list of external tutorials rather than code. It is organized by the technology being rebuilt (for example 3D Renderer, Database, Docker, Shell, Programming Language, Operating System, Web Server, Neural Network), and each section lists guides with the language they use, such as C, Go, Rust, Python, or JavaScript. Some entries are marked as video or PDF. An Uncategorized section holds guides that do not fit a single category, like the NAND to Tetris course and a DNS server guide. The README states the premise that understanding comes from building things yourself, and it invites pull requests for new submissions.
use_cases: find a tutorial for building my own database or Redis clone
learn compilers or interpreters by writing one
follow a guide to write a shell or terminal emulator
find step-by-step projects for building a web server from scratch
learn how Docker or containers work by rebuilding them
find beginner game or emulator tutorials in my language
notable: Organized by technology to rebuild, with the implementation language listed for each tutorial
Covers a wide range of topics, from Lisp interpreters and Game Boy emulators to neural networks and blockchains
Accepts community submissions through pull requests and issues
Maintained by CodeCrafters, Inc. after being started by Daniel Stefanovic
caveats: Links point to third-party tutorials, so their quality, availability, and freshness vary and are not verified here
Contains no code of its own and nothing to install or run
summary.license: The README says the contributors have waived copyright to the extent possible under law (CC0-style dedication), but it does not name a license explicitly.
keywords: build a neural network from scratch
